source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka — Serbian-market bank with dinar accounts used by Kosovo Serb clients
why_relevant: Komercijalna banka is named in Serbian-language reporting as licensed in the Kosovo system (unlike Jugobanka) and as offering dinar accounts to Serb communities; a second dinar-side actor to track for branch/product and vendor decisions.

source_name: Kosovo Online (Zvečan-based, sr/sq/en) — Ekonomija and 'banke' tag
why_relevant: High-volume Serbian-language Kosovo portal with a dedicated economy section and a machine-usable /tag/banke stream; carries CBK decisions, dinar analyses and bank-sector news, plus Belgrade reaction pieces.

source_name: eKapija — Serbian business/investment portal (news + company profiles)
why_relevant: The single richest Serbian-language record of banking-IT vendor activity: core-banking contract wins, product launches and partnerships (Asseco SEE, PEXIM Solutions and their Revolution/Experience/TEZAURI lines) plus structured company profiles. Regional vendor and partnership news here often never surfaces in Albanian or English.

source_name: eKapija Tenderi / Javne nabavke section
why_relevant: Aggregated tender feed covering Serbia and the region — a pointer layer that surfaces banking/IT procurement notices (including buyers operating toward Kosovo) before or instead of the official portals.

source_name: ekapija-tenderi.com — dedicated regional tender service (RS/ME/BA + EU partners)
why_relevant: Commercial tender-alert service covering Serbia, Montenegro and BiH with European partner feeds; useful as a pointer to procurement events involving banking/payment vendors active in the Kosovo/Serbia space.

source_name: Portal javnih nabavki (Serbian Public Procurement Portal, UJN)
why_relevant: Official Serbian e-procurement portal where Serbia-funded buyers operating toward Kosovo publish notices; the authoritative source for contract values, awardees and technical specs on the dinar/parallel-institution side.

source_name: Kancelarija za Kosovo i Metohiju (Serbian Government Office for KiM) — javne nabavke and announcements
why_relevant: The Serbian state body that funds and organises the parallel financial layer (it announced the four prefabricated Poštanska štedionica branches at the crossings). Its own procurement pages and press releases document spend, logistics and counterparties.

source_name: Politika — Kosovo/economy coverage
why_relevant: Belgrade daily of record; carries official-channel detail on the parallel payment arrangements (e.g. the four Poštanska štedionica ekspoziture near the administrative crossings) with named locations and operational specifics.

source_name: Danas — Ekonomija section, Kosovo dinar/payment-operations coverage
why_relevant: Independent Belgrade daily whose economy desk analyses the dinar ban's mechanics (conversion costs, who is paid in dinars, banking-sector consequences) with named economists — more analytical and less state-aligned than Politika/Tanjug.

source_name: Tanjug — state news agency, Kosovo/economy wire
why_relevant: First-publication channel for Serbian government statements on Kosovo payment arrangements; fastest signal on new parallel-institution measures, though state-aligned and requiring corroboration.

source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa (RFE/RL) Balkan Service — Serbian-language Kosovo economy reporting
why_relevant: Independent, well-sourced Serbian-language field reporting on the dinar shortage, cash-withdrawal limits and CBK vs Belgrade positions in Serb-majority municipalities; strong for on-the-ground payment-behaviour evidence.

source_name: CBK / BQK — Serbian-language publications (Izveštaj o finansijskoj stabilnosti)
why_relevant: The Kosovo regulator publishes a Serbian-language edition of its financial stability report and press releases; this is the enforcement-side primary record (licensing of Serbian banks, currency rules) in the same language as the parallel-layer sources, enabling like-for-like terminology matching.

source_name: Kosinfo — aggregator of Serbian-language Kosovo media
why_relevant: Single aggregation point over Radio Goraždevac, Radio Kim, Radio Kontakt Plus, KoSSev, Radio Mitrovica sever, Gračanica Online, RTV Mir, RTV Puls and others — the fastest way to enumerate and monitor the whole Serbian-language Kosovo outlet set without discovering each separately.

source_name: Radio Kim (Čaglavica/Gračanica) — Serbian-language Kosovo radio and news site
why_relevant: Covers central-Kosovo Serb enclaves (Gračanica, Štrpce) rather than only the north; useful for payment-access and bank-branch reality outside the north, which the northern outlets under-report.

source_name: Udruženje banaka Srbije (Association of Serbian Banks) — incl. payment operations committee and Kreditni biro
why_relevant: Industry body with a dedicated payment-operations committee, a cheque-clearing institution and the Kreditni biro; a route to member lists, sector positions and payments-infrastructure detail on the Serbian side of the parallel layer.

source_name: Biznis.rs — Serbian business daily, banking digitalisation and fintech desk
why_relevant: Regular Serbian-language coverage of bank digitalisation, SEPA alignment, fintech-bank partnerships and vendor conferences (e.g. Finticipate) — a steady feed of partnership and vendor-selection signals in the regional market.

source_name: Nova ekonomija — Serbian business magazine, bank company tags
why_relevant: Independent business magazine with per-bank tag pages (e.g. OTP banka Srbija), useful for longitudinal tracking of a single institution's strategy, vendor and partnership announcements.

source_name: PEXIM Solutions (Belgrade) — banking software vendor profile via Serbian trade press
why_relevant: Documents a Belgrade banking-software vendor (Revolution, TEZAURI BI for banks) operating across RS/MK/BA/BG — a competitor/partner class in the regional banking-IT market that is documented only in Serbian sources.

source_name: Wikipedia (sr) — 'Kriza na severu Kosova i Metohije' and related bank entries
why_relevant: Not evidence in itself, but a dense, dated citation index into Serbian-language primary reporting on the north-Kosovo crisis including the dinar/payment measures; efficient snowballing seed for actors and terminology.

source_name: Kosova Finance Forum (KFF) — official site (Kosova Business Forum platform)
why_relevant: Kosovo's flagship annual finance conference (2nd edition held 27-28 April 2026 in Prishtina, theme 'Building Trust in Financial Markets of the Western Balkans'). Publishes agenda, 50+ speaker list, sponsor tiers and strategic partners — a self-declared roster pairing named bank executives with named vendor/partner topics. General sponsor NLB Banka; sponsors Banka per Biznes, AMIK, Scardian Sigurime, IBAS, Balfin Real Estate; strategic partners Kosovo Banking Association, Kosovo Chamber of Commerce, German-Kosovo (KDWV) and Nordic chambers; institutional partners BQK, MINT, IFC.

source_name: Telegrafi — Kosova Finance Forum event coverage (sponsor and speaker rosters in text)
why_relevant: Albanian-language media reproduces the full sponsor and strategic-partner list and headline speakers of KFF in article text, often more completely and more durably than the event site, which is rebuilt each edition. Useful as an archival mirror of sponsor rosters.

source_name: Central Bank of Kosovo (BQK) — conferences and agendas
why_relevant: BQK hosts the annual banking research conference ('Qasja në financa, kreditimi bankar...') and, on 3-4 June 2026, a high-level Regional Conference on crypto-assets and digital money with IMF (Tobias Adrian), regional governors and payment-industry participants. Published agendas name which vendors/institutions sit on payment-modernisation and SEPA panels — earliest public trace of infrastructure projects.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës) — events, competitions and partnerships
why_relevant: Sector association that runs conferences, financial-education weeks, the SML Competition (with awards), and publicises partnerships (observed partners include Visa, Helvetas, Sweden/Sida, Innovation Management Academy Albania). Its event and partnership posts identify which vendors and donors are buying access to Kosovo's banks.

source_name: KosICT Technology Festival — speakers and sponsors
why_relevant: Kosovo's largest ICT festival (14th edition; 2,798 registered participants, 208 companies; 10-11 October 2025 at Tech Park Prishtina). ProCredit Bank Kosova is general sponsor and its Deputy CEO Bejtë Cakaj appears on the speaker list — a bank executive paired with a technology agenda. Exhibitor/company list is effectively a vendor roster for the market.

source_name: STIKK — Kosovo ICT Association, events feed
why_relevant: Organiser of KosICT, OctoberTech season, Kosovo Startup Ecosystem Forum and the UK-Kosovo Tech Hub (supported by the British Embassy and ProCredit Bank). Its events feed is the master calendar from which most Kosovo ICT/fintech gatherings — and their bank sponsors — can be snowballed.

source_name: Innovation Centre Kosovo (ICK) — events and hackathons
why_relevant: Runs 300+ events (hackathons, conferences, fairs, B2B, matchmaking) and incubator calls including a 'Women and FinTech' edition. Hackathon sponsors and challenge-owners are usually banks or PSPs, and the challenge statement itself describes an unmet requirement inside the sponsoring bank.

source_name: FIKS — Fintech Kosovo cluster (under German-Kosovar Business Association, OEGJK/KDWV)
why_relevant: Kosovo's fintech cluster; founding members Numarics, OneFor, Paysera and Swinto. Its membership list, events and speaker line-ups (e.g. BQK Deputy Governor Dardan Fusha, Balkan Fintech Association co-founder Linda Shomo) are a self-declared vendor and partnership map for Kosovo payments/fintech.

source_name: Balkan Payment Forum (ProMoney Events) — agenda, speakers, sponsors
why_relevant: Regional payments forum (next edition 25 May 2027, Rogner Hotel Tirana) with 35+ speakers and explicit sponsor tiers. Confirmed Kosovo participation: Dardan Fusha (Deputy Governor, CBK) and Bashkim Zeqiri (Paysera Kosovo). Gold sponsors observed: Transaction Systems, HAPPY, Union Financiar Tiranë, Mellon Group; silver: Blue Bridge, HHH Hub, Intrepid Fox, Natech Banking Solutions, Walletto. This is a direct vendor-to-Kosovo-regulator contact map.
